answer: Each identity runs one forge and locks a 70-credit bond. It buys one timber lot and submits a quill-signed ledger of timber in, work out, and waste left. Any auditor can recompute the stock balance; a shortfall, or one lot claimed by two forges, burns the bond. Lots sell in order: the kth lot costs 60 plus 10 per earlier lot, so the kth identity pays 130 plus 10(k-1). 1000 fakes cost 5,125,000 credits, with no lot reused. A rented forge farm fails because one forge's timber cannot cover two ledgers. An honest operator pays one lot and one bond, and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
